parts.label: a
parts.technique: Linear interpolation for median from grouped frequency data
parts.reason: S2.3 covers linear interpolation for percentiles/median from grouped data.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Estimate mean from grouped frequency data
parts.reason: S2.3 covers measures of central tendency including mean, using summary statistics.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Estimate standard deviation using Sxx formula
parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly permits calculating standard deviation from summary statistics using Sxx.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Probability from grouped frequency data using interpolation
parts.reason: Combines S2.3 interpolation with basic probability estimation (S3.1), no excluded content involved.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Range from box plot
parts.reason: S2.1 covers box plots and interpretation.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: IQR from box plot
parts.reason: S2.1 covers box plot interpretation including quartiles.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Skewness from quartiles
parts.reason: S2.1/S2.3 cover interpretation of box plots and measures of variation; comparing quartile spacing to assess skew is standard interpretation.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Calculate PMCC using Sxx, Sxt, Stt formula
parts.reason: S5.1 explicitly excludes calculation of correlation coefficients using the formula; this requires exactly that.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Interpret computed correlation coefficient
parts.reason: Depends directly on the excluded PMCC formula calculation in (d); the part only makes sense after that out-of-spec calculation.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Identify outliers and redraw box plot
parts.reason: S2.4 covers identifying outliers using specified rules and box plot representation.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Normal distribution probability calculation
parts.reason: S4.2 covers using the Normal distribution to find probabilities; no pdf knowledge required.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Inverse normal to find a percentile
parts.reason: S4.2 covers finding probabilities/values with Normal distribution, including simultaneous equation type problems.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Conditional probability with Normal distribution (median of truncated distribution)
parts.reason: Uses standard Normal distribution inverse calculation methods covered by S4.2; no pdf derivation required.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Normal probability combined with independent event probability
parts.reason: S4.2 for normal probability and S3.1 for independent events multiplication.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Tree diagram, solve for unknown probability using total probability
parts.reason: S3.2 covers tree diagrams and conditional probability relations.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Tree diagram algebra to find unknown probability
parts.reason: S3.2 covers tree diagrams, conditional probability formula application.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Compute probability of event from tree diagram
parts.reason: S3.2 covers computing probabilities using tree diagrams.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Conditional probability formula
parts.reason: S3.2 explicitly covers conditional probability formula P(A|B).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Calculate Sss (sum of squares) statistic
parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly permits use of the Sxx-type statistic for calculating standard deviation; the same computational technique is used here, not the PMCC formula.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Interpret given correlation coefficient value re suitability of linear model
parts.reason: S2.2 covers informal interpretation of correlation without requiring the PMCC formula; value of r is given, not calculated by the student.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Identify explanatory variable
parts.reason: S2.2 covers terms explanatory/response variable and reasoning about causal direction.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Find Sst using the PMCC formula r = Sst/√(SssStt)
parts.reason: S5.1 explicitly states use of the PMCC formula is not required/excluded; this method requires exactly that formula.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Calculate linear regression equation
parts.reason: S2.2 explicitly excludes calculations involving regression lines.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Standard deviation calculation
parts.reason: S2.3 covers standard deviation calculation from summary statistics; independent of the excluded regression parts.

parts.label: g
parts.technique: Use regression equation to estimate value
parts.reason: Depends directly on the excluded regression equation calculated in (e); calculations involving regression lines are excluded.

parts.label: h
parts.technique: Comment on reliability of regression estimate (extrapolation)
parts.reason: Depends on the out-of-spec regression estimate from (g); regression-line calculations are excluded even though extrapolation concept itself is mentioned in S2.2 guidance.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Show probability value for discrete distribution (geometric-type)
parts.reason: S4.1 covers understanding and using simple discrete probability distributions (excluding mean/variance calculation only); finding a probability value itself is in spec.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Complete discrete probability distribution table
parts.reason: S4.1 covers use of simple discrete probability distributions; finding probabilities (not mean/variance) is permitted.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Calculate E(X) of a general discrete random variable
parts.reason: S4.1 explicitly excludes calculation of mean and variance of discrete random variables.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Calculate Var(X) of a general discrete random variable
parts.reason: S4.1 explicitly excludes calculation of mean and variance of discrete random variables.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Determine probability distribution of related discrete random variable H
parts.reason: S4.1 covers understanding and use of simple discrete probability distributions; this is constructing a distribution, not computing mean/variance.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Find intersection probabilities from discrete distributions
parts.reason: S3.1/S4.1 cover probability calculations with discrete distributions; no mean/variance involved.

parts.label: g
parts.technique: Find probability distribution of S = X + H
parts.reason: S4.1 covers use of simple discrete probability distributions; constructing the distribution table is permitted, distinct from the excluded mean/variance calculation.
